title: Process of Welding Metals Electrically (US Patent No. 428,459)
locator: Letters Patent No. 428,459; application filed 1890-03-07, Serial No. 342,975; patented 1890-05-20; full specification + 2 claims
why: THE LOAD-BEARING DOCUMENT. Signed "CHARLES L. COFFIN", "of Detroit, in the county of Wayne and State of Michigan". Claim 2 is the one the histories point at: the ends of the rods "may be slightly separated from the carbon after the current is established, thus forming a voltaic arc". Text is the Google Patents OCR reproduced verbatim; that OCR mangles the surname in the running heads ("OOFFIN"/"OOPFIN"/"OOF'PIN"/"UOFFIN") and nothing was silently corrected. Independently confirmed by src-0003-og-vol51-1890 entry [C].

title: Process of Electric Welding (US Patent No. 395,878)
locator: Letters Patent No. 395,878; application filed 1888-09-18, Serial No. 285,742; patented 1889-01-08; full specification + 1 claim
why: EARLIER THAN 428,459 AND IT IS THE ONE THAT SAYS "FILLER METAL": the claim is welding "by subjecting the articles to the action of a voltaic arc of which one pole is metal conductor, fusing said conductor, depositing the molten metal on the joint". Signed "CHARLES L. COFFIN, of Detroit". Google Patents OCR verbatim; running head OCRs as "COPPIN"/"(OFFIN", uncorrected.

title: Official Gazette of the United States Patent Office, Vol. 51 (April-June 1890) -- the Charles L. Coffin entries
locator: item officialgazette51unit, file officialgazette51unit_djvu.txt; body entries for patents 425,164 / 427,971 / 428,459 and the volume Index of Patentees (djvu.txt lines 35779-35790, 167528-167537, 190534-190553, 332709-332717)
why: The Patent Office's own record of issuance. HOW 425,164 AND 427,971 WERE IDENTIFIED AS HIS AT ALL: the volume Index of Patentees carries three lines reading "Coffin, Charles L., Detroit, Mich.", and scanning the body of the same volume returns exactly three matching entries -- the count agrees, so the attribution is the Office's, not a secondary list's. OVERLAP: the claims printed under entry 428,459 are the same two claims as src-0001; one piece of evidence, not two. OCR CAUTION: the 428,459 header OCRs as "428.469" (position between the 428,458 and 428,460 entries plus a word-for-word title/claim match is what fixes the number) and its serial OCRs as "848,971" where the patent prints 342,975. Left uncorrected in the file.

title: Method of Electric Welding (US Patent No. 425,164)
locator: Letters Patent No. 425,164; application filed 1889-11-06, Serial No. 329,394; patented 1890-04-08; specification + 3 claims
why: Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." Claim 3 combines both ideas he is remembered for in one sentence: traversing the joint with a voltaic arc AND "re-enforcing the joint by supplying like metal carried by the traversing conductor and fused by the arc". Attribution comes from the Patent Office's own index, not a secondary list -- see src-0003. OCR CAUTION: a column header on the last PDF page OCRs as "425,162"; the patent is 425,164. Uncorrected.

title: Method of Electric Welding (US Patent No. 427,971)
locator: Letters Patent No. 427,971; application filed 1889-04-24; patented 1890-05-13; specification + 1 claim
why: Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." The single claim protects the arc and the work "by a jacket of non-conducting refractory material" -- shielding, three decades before coated electrodes were routine. Same-day-family as 409,015 (both filed 1889-04-24).

title: Electric Welding (US Patent No. 409,015)
locator: Letters Patent No. 409,015; application filed 1889-04-24; patented 1889-08-13
why: Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." Filed the same day as 427,971 but issued nine months earlier.

title: Electric Welding (US Patent No. 477,101)
locator: Letters Patent No. 477,101; application filed 1889-11-06, Serial No. 329,393; patented 1892-06-14
why: Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." Serial 329,393 is the number immediately BELOW 425,164's serial 329,394 -- the two were filed together on 1889-11-06 and then took two and a half years apart to issue.

title: Electric Metal-Working (US Patent No. 483,427)
locator: Letters Patent No. 483,427; application filed 1892-02-06, Serial No. 420,487; patented 1892-09-27
why: Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." The title widens from "welding" to "metal-working" -- the same widening that later names his company.

title: Apparatus for Electric Welding (US Patent No. 495,393)
locator: Letters Patent No. 495,393; application filed 1891-06-11; patented 1893-04-11; 3 sheets of drawings
why: Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." An APPARATUS patent, not a process one -- machine detail rather than principle. Paired with 495,394, issued the same day. The scan OCRs "PATENT OFFICE" as "PATENT @rricn", which is why the identity line in this file's header was quoted by hand.

title: Machine for Electrically Welding Metals (US Patent No. 495,394)
locator: Letters Patent No. 495,394; application filed 1892-08-06, Serial No. 442,336; patented 1893-04-11
why: Header OCRs as "cHARLEs IQ. COFFIN, on DETROIT, MICHIGAN"; the body reads "Be it known that I, CHARLES L. COFFIN, of Detroit, in the county of Wayne and State of Michigan". Issued the same day as 495,393.

title: Process of Treating Ore Containing Lead, Silver, and Zinc (US Patent No. 442,016)
why: NOT A WELDING PATENT, and admitted deliberately. Header: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN, ASSIGNOR OF ONE-HALF TO GEORGE H. LOTHROP, OF SAME PLACE." A Lothrop witnesses two of his welding patents ("GEO. H. LOTHROP" on 428,459, "HENRY B. LOTHROP" on 395,878), so the name corroborates that this is the same Detroit man rather than a third Coffin. It is also the only evidence in the corpus that his interests ran to metallurgy generally.

title: Electric Metal-Working Apparatus (US Patent No. 646,619)
locator: Letters Patent No. 646,619; application filed 1899-05-13; patented 1900-04-03
why: The only document in the corpus that states his CITIZENSHIP: "Be it known that I, CHARLES L. COFFIN, a citizen of the United States, residing ...". Header still reads "OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN", so he is in Detroit as late as the 1899 filing.

title: Metallic Barrel (US Patent No. 845,760)
locator: Letters Patent No. 845,760; application filed 1906-04-02, Serial No. 309,561; patented 1907-03-05
why: THE ROW THAT MOVES HIM OUT OF MICHIGAN: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF NACOOCHEE, GEORGIA, ASSIGNOR TO ELECTRIC METAL WORKING COMPANY, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN, A CORPORATION OF MICHIGAN." From here on the Detroit tie is the company's, not his address. Also shows what the welding process was being sold to do by 1906: seamless welded metal barrels.

title: Method of Electric-Arc Welding, Heating, and Metal-Working, and Apparatus Therefor (US Patent No. 1,216,947)
locator: Letters Patent No. 1,216,947; application filed 1916-04-05; patented 1917-02-20; 7 PDF pages
why: "CHARLES L. COFFIN, OF PARKS, GEORGIA, ASSIGNOR TO ELECTRIC METAL WORKING COMPANY, OF DETROIT, MICHIGAN." Twenty-seven years after 428,459 and he is still filing on arc welding. Much longer and more discursive than the 1889-93 specifications.

title: Art of Arc Welding, Heating, and the Like (US Patent No. 1,265,613)
locator: Letters Patent No. 1,265,613; application filed 1918-04-01, Serial No. 89,130; patented 1918-05-07; 8 PDF pages
why: THE LATEST DOCUMENT IN THIS CORPUS and the longest. Header OCRs as "CHARLES L. COFI'IN, 01' PABKS, GEORGIA" (= OF PARKS, GEORGIA), assignor to Electric Metal Working Company of Detroit. Establishes he was alive and working in 1918; says nothing about a death year.

title: List of Works in the New York Public Library Relating to Electric Welding, comp. William B. Gamble (New York, 1913) -- the Coffin entries
locator: item listworksrelati00deptgoog, file listworksrelati00deptgoog_djvu.txt; all 17 occurrences of "Coffin", each with surrounding context, at djvu.txt lines given inline
why: THE ONLY NON-PRIMARY ROW HERE, and the only contemporaneous evidence of how his work was RECEIVED. A research library's chronological bibliography of the world literature on electric welding to 1913. It records a named "Coffin process" / "Coffin arc process" being described in English, French and German periodicals from 1890 to 1911 alongside Benardos, Slavianoff, Thomson, Zerener, Lagrange-Hoho and Ries; and it records that the Coffin patent was publicly CONTESTED in 1890 (annotation under A. M. Tanner, "Electric blowpipes", Telegraphic Journal & Electrical Review, London, v. 27, 1890-09-19). NAMESAKE CHECK: all 17 occurrences attach the name to a welding process, never to company affairs; Thomson and "Thomson-Houston" appear in the same bibliography as separate competing processes, which is itself evidence the two Coffins are different men.

title: "A New Method of Electric Welding" [cut captioned "Coffin's Incandescent Welder"], The Electrical World (New York), v. XVI no. 12, 1890-09-20, p. 196
why: Found by following a citation in src-0016, not by guessing. NAMESAKE CHECK: names him as "Chas. L. Coffin, of De-/troit, Mich." and talks only about welding apparatus. IMPORTANT FOR THE PICTURE OF HIM: this is his INCANDESCENT (resistance) welder, a different branch from the arc patents -- he worked both. Carries experimental detail found nowhere in the patents: welding under vacuum saves about 50 per cent of the energy at a vacuum of one-tenth to one-twelfth, and a fractured piece rejoined in vacuum welds "at a low red heat". Unsigned journalism, so S1 even though the detail reads as inventor-supplied -- no byline claim is made. OCR CAUTION: the metal/alloy tables are multi-column and the OCR interleaves and corrupts them; do not quote them as a clean list.

title: "Electric Arc Welding and Metal Working", The Electrical World (New York), v. XXII no. 1, 1893-07-01, p. 14
why: Also found via a citation in src-0016. NAMESAKE CHECK: "invented by Charles L. Coffin, of Detroit, who has made a specialty of this branch of electricity". Shows what the processes had become commercially by 1893: rod/bar/axle, strap and bridge-strap, tire, sheet and tube welders. ★ THE ARTICLE'S OWN ARITHMETIC DOES NOT AGREE: it claims welds average "98.6 per cent. of tke original tensile strength" but the only figures it prints -- eight bars at 47,719 lb/sq in welded against 49,264 unwelded -- work out to 96.9 per cent. Both left exactly as scanned; neither adjusted to fit the other. ★★ THE SLICE IS NOT PURE: multi-column OCR jumped into a neighbouring article on an electric-railway conduit contact shoe (roughly source lines 5446-5473); that text is NOT about Coffin and was left in rather than silently deleted so the slice still matches the source line for line.
